mbm-0901.clue: My slippers know the theme song.
mbm-0901.quote: On Friday nights my sister and I make our fuzzy slippers dance when the detective show starts. Last week Mum filmed the slippers and missed the culprit’s big entrance.

mbm-0902.clue: I found a tiny mountain on the gym floor.
mbm-0902.quote: Chalk scattered under my bar in a shape like our local ridge. I drew a little flag at the summit with one finger after my final rep. My spotter wanted a photo before we swept.

mbm-0903.clue: My band rehearses with a spare lampshade.
mbm-0903.quote: We put a red lampshade over a little work light to give the garage a stage glow. Now when the bass starts rattling the fringe, everybody knows we’ve found the groove.

mbm-0904.clue: I fixed a bug by following a duck.
mbm-0904.quote: I wrote a pond game where one little duck kept walking backward. I traced its footsteps on graph paper and found I’d reversed the two directions. My sister asked me to give that duck its own level.

mbm-0905.clue: I like a staircase with a story.
mbm-0905.quote: My guidebook mentioned a hundred steps. I counted a hundred and one because a doorstep at the bottom held a bowl of oranges and its owner invited me to sit down.

mbm-0906.clue: I wear my grandmother’s kitchen floor on my knees.
mbm-0906.quote: I copied her old checkerboard tiles into a lap quilt. The blue square with the yellow corner marks the spot where she dropped a jar of mustard the summer I learned to cook.

mbm-0907.clue: I know who owns the long blue pawn.
mbm-0907.quote: We ran out of pieces at games night and my uncle volunteered a blue crayon. Every square he crossed got a tiny streak. We could retrace his entire winning route after supper.

mbm-0908.clue: I saved the last dance for the coat-check girl.
mbm-0908.quote: Her shift ended during our favorite chorus. We danced in the little square between the coat racks, with winter scarves brushing our shoulders on every turn.

mbm-0909.clue: I pressed the corn leaves myself.
mbm-0909.quote: At harvest we rubbed leaf shapes onto scrap paper. I used them as templates for our kitchen quilt. One of the green leaves is upside down because my brother insisted that’s how he held it.

mbm-0910.clue: My belt has a tiny door.
mbm-0910.quote: I tooled a little cottage on the back of a leather belt and made the door a stitched flap. Behind it is an acorn. The belt is for my niece, who says somebody very small lives there.

mbm-0911.clue: I once tuned a string to a bird.
mbm-0911.quote: I was tuning my cuatro by the kitchen window when a finch kept answering the high string. Mum recorded us on cassette. You can hear me stop playing to give the bird its solo.

mbm-0912.clue: My notebook comes with a free umbrella.
mbm-0912.quote: Rain washed half a sentence off the page while I was writing by the bus stop. The words that stayed made a better ending. I circled them and drew the dripping roof above them.

mbm-0913.clue: I turned the spare pocket inside out.
mbm-0913.quote: I stitched a quilt from the aprons our family wore at the market. In the red pocket I found a little wooden clothes peg. I tucked it back in before I finished the seam.

mbm-0914.clue: I can still hear the tin cans singing.
mbm-0914.quote: Our homemade mini-golf hole runs through a tunnel of painted cans. The only time I scored from the porch, it sounded like a tiny marching band coming down the path.

mbm-0915.clue: I bring a pencil for the mileposts.
mbm-0915.quote: My little brother drew faces for each rest stop on our hike. At the lookout I added a pair of glasses to the happiest one. That’s where we shared my last pear.

mbm-0916.clue: I tucked a spoon into my life vest.
mbm-0916.quote: My sister and I canoed across the pond with a jar of pudding between us. At the island we discovered one spoon. We took turns and stayed all afternoon.

mbm-0917.clue: I know where the smallest bridge goes.
mbm-0917.quote: The big bridge was thick with sightseers. A tiny footbridge took me to a tailor’s yard, where six bright red jackets dried above the water. That’s the view I ended up drawing.

mbm-0918.clue: My blanket has a page you can turn.
mbm-0918.quote: I quilted an open storybook into the center. A fabric page lifts to show the mouse hiding on the next page. My niece always skips right to the mouse.

mbm-0919.clue: I can find north in our hangar.
mbm-0919.quote: A retired pilot painted a compass on the floor beneath the training plane. I took a rubbing of the north arrow before we repainted it. The red mark still peeks through the paper.

mbm-0920.clue: I putt better when the crocodile smiles.
mbm-0920.quote: Our old mini-golf crocodile lost one wooden tooth. The gap is just wide enough for a lucky shot. I only made it once, while my nephew was busy drawing in a replacement.

mbm-0921.clue: I made a harvest moon out of a sleeve.
mbm-0921.quote: My sister’s orange dress was too torn to wear again. I cut one sleeve into a moon for her quilt. The cuff became the little porch light underneath it.

mbm-0922.clue: I have an unfair advantage at word games.
mbm-0922.quote: We lost the letter bag and used my wool hat. Every time somebody drew a tile it came out wearing a bit of green fluff. My mum awarded an extra point for the fluffiest word.

mbm-0923.clue: I know where the stars go when it rains.
mbm-0923.quote: Our campsite clouded over, so we punched constellations in an empty tin and shone a flashlight through it. The stars came back on the tent wall, close enough to touch.

mbm-0924.clue: I quilt my mistakes into pockets.
mbm-0924.quote: I cut a patch too narrow for the middle of my blanket. It made a perfect pocket along the edge. There’s a chocolate coin in it for the first visitor who finds it.

mbm-0925.clue: I save the tickets from bad movies.
mbm-0925.quote: My cousin and I redraw the endings on the backs of the stubs. My favorite is a terrible sea-monster movie where our version ends with the monster opening a swimming school.
